# The suite's rules

`npm test` checks these first, with every run (`node suite-rules/check.mjs`, no browser, well under a
second), and then runs the tests whatever they say. Run them alone: `npm run rules` (in the-internet-herokuapp-com-cypress-tests).

Each rule has a **tier**:

- **hard**: the suite's own integrity, and a test that checks nothing. Broken, it fails the run.
- **story**: how a story is written. It holds for stories only (a spec that calls `story()`) and
  fails the run like a hard rule. A spec of your own with plain `it()` tests is held to the hard
  rules only.
- **advisory**: the suite's conventions. Broken, it is a warning in the run's output and in
  `cypress/rules-report.md`, whose first line counts the warnings (for CI to gate on, if a team wants).

The rule ids are the same in every suite Suite Builder writes (Playwright, Selenium, Cypress).

| Rule | Tier | What must be true | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SR-01 | story | A story is in cypress/e2e/cases/ | One folder holds every story, the generated tests beside them; a spec of your own that is not a story may live anywhere under cypress/e2e/. |
| SR-02 | story | A story is written with story() (holds by how a story is written) | A story is a spec that calls story() (G-119): a spec that does not is a test of your own, held to the hard rules only, so no story is written without it. |
| SR-03 | story | A story names its story (holds by how a story is written) | story('&lt;id>', '&lt;title>', () => ...) cannot be written without the story's id: SR-02, which asks for story(), asks for the id too. |
| SR-04 | story | A story's file is named after its id | Finding the test of a story, or the story of a test, is then a file name, not a search. |
| SR-05 | story | Each story id is used once | Two tests for one story (or one requirement of it, PROJ-1-3) report it twice, and the tracker can't tell which one speaks for it. |
| SR-06 | advisory | A story is one test | One story states one outcome: one story() call, with no it() or describe() of its own beside it. |
| SR-07 | advisory | A story has one check | A story's test proves its one outcome with one .verify() at the end of its chain. |
| SR-08 | advisory | The check comes last | The check is the story's outcome: a step after it is a second story hiding in the first. |
| SR-09 | advisory | A story's test reads as its title (holds by how a story is written) | story() names the test with the story's title, so the report and the run's output read as the story. |
| SR-10 | story | A story uses page objects, not Cypress | A story reads like the story because every step is a page method named for what a visitor does ("click().learnMore()"). |
| SR-11 | advisory | A story does not assert | Checks live in the pages' verify() methods, built on Checks, which log the step and fail in plain English. |
| SR-12 | advisory | Nothing sleeps | cy.wait(2000) is slow on a fast day and too short on a slow one. |
| SR-13 | advisory | No regular expressions in tests and pages | Expected texts and addresses are plain strings: a person reads them at a glance, and a regular expression that looks right can quietly match the wrong thing. |
| SR-14 | advisory | A test switched off says why | A test skipped without a word passes in every report and is forgotten; with its reason on the line, the next person knows whether it can come back. |
| SR-15 | hard | YOURS blocks keep both marker lines | Regenerating keeps what is between the marker lines: a block missing one of them is lost, or swallows the rest of the file. |
| SR-16 | hard | Generated files change only inside YOURS blocks | Everything outside the blocks is rewritten by the next rebuild, the rules included: an edit there is lost. |
| SR-17 | story | Every story in stories/done/ has its test | A story marked done without a test is a promise nothing keeps. |
| SR-18 | story | Every story test has its story in stories/done/ | A test whose story is gone tests something nobody asked for any more, or its story was lost. |
| SR-19 | hard | Every test checks something | A test that only acts passes whenever nothing throws: it can't tell the right page from the wrong one. |
| SR-20 | hard | Account files stay out of git | An account in git is an account everyone with the repository has: the account files in secrets/ are each person's own, written blank in every fresh copy (G-159). |
| SR-21 | story | A done story's notes name every criterion, by its number | A criterion's number is its test's name (&lt;id>-&lt;n>): a list edited after its tests were written moves every number after the edit, so a test checks one criterion under another's number, and a criterion left out of the notes is a part of the story nobody checks, or says is unchecked (trial 7: 3 of 3 list edits renumbered tested stories). |
| SR-22 | hard | One element, one name | Every test then reaches one element two ways, and a locator fixed under one name is still broken under the other; two stories written apart (two branches) each add their own name for the same button and merge without a conflict. |

Every rule in full, with how to fix a failure: [ai/rules-in-full.md](ai/rules-in-full.md).

The rules files (suite-rules/check.mjs, this file and `suite-rules/fingerprints.txt`) are generated with
the suite. A change to one is a change outside a YOURS block: regenerating overwrites it, SR-16
reports it, and `suite verify the-internet-herokuapp-com-cypress-tests` finds it. To change a rule, change Suite Builder.
